scope: Independent semantic read of the two parent-authored ActualMass/Canonical ridge adapters, six declarations. Exact canonical point, mass and individual-incidence coefficient conversion only.

authorship.independence_limit: This is an independent proof-body review of the parent two sources and their application of the imported APIs. It is not a new second read of the reviewer-authored imported proof bodies.

supporting_definitions_read.scope: Canonical conormal definition and proved unit/span/ridge-zero/strict-positive properties, for orientation checking.
Canonical mass API and actual complete-face input conditions.

semantic_checks.finding: The selected boundary ON3 frame spans the original three selected normals by the imported frame API. All three lie in the actual H normal space because their indices are proved active in H. Span inclusion plus ON3 finrank=3 and H actual normal rank=3 prove equality; no restriction to exactly three active original facets is introduced.

The native normal point and canonical H normal point are both in the same selected-three-normal span. Actual original supporting levels for j,l,index(i) and the canonical face supporting levels allow the checked normal-point uniqueness theorem to prove equality. Equal-point and equal-span identities are conclusions, not premises.

The local mass is first the actual full-original-event native frame hard mass from the core Mass API. The canonical mass theorem is instantiated with the actual ON3 frame, derived H span and derived point equality. All H-active and all inactive original closed constraints are retained; no covariance-only or marginal-only substitution is used.

In the conormal adapter, I is an actual codimension-two face incident to H, and its complete active set is exactly {j,l}. P.retained proves the selected third index is neither j nor l. Together with its membership in H this supplies the strict H-outside-R orientation needed by conormal uniqueness.

The canonical incident conormal is unit, belongs to H normal space, and vanishes on the ridge normals. The original-normal sum/difference formulas then give zero pairing with both native pair frame vectors. Derived frame-span equality places that canonical conormal in the actual native boundary frame span, satisfying every imported uniqueness hypothesis.

The sign is correct. The supporting canonical definition is minus the normalized H-space projection of the direction from an H relative-interior point toward an R relative-interior point. That direction has negative pairing with every H-active normal outside R, so the canonical conormal has positive pairing there and points out of the ridge. The adapter uses that positivity rather than assuming an orientation identity.

The signed support distance is recovered by testing the canonical H normal-space point on j,l,index(i). Its actual supporting levels yield the native pair coordinate levels and the selected tangent support level. This argument does not assume that the projected normal-space point lies in the original polyhedron.

Substitution of the proved conormal equality and real inner-product symmetry gives precisely d_i=<z_H,n_RH>, preserving its sign. There is no absolute-value replacement or missing sign from the outward orientation.

The coefficient adapter multiplies the proved signed distance by the actual native weight arccos(dot uj ul)*phi(alpha)*phi(beta) and selected boundary mass. The proved canonical mass identity converts the complete density product once, leaving arccos(dot uj ul)*(<z_H,n_RH>*rho_H). There is no additional Gram denominator, normal-length Jacobian, or ordered-pair factor 1/2 at this individual-incidence stage.

All six declarations have fixed-threshold geometric inputs only. They do not assume a Green/surface estimate, common mass equality, normal-point equality, conormal equality, a full-family independence hypothesis, threshold genericity or a limiting/Fatou continuation.

limitations: The selected-facet/canonical-H incidence bijection and coverage/counting are not supplied by these two sources and are not certified here.
